title: openai/codex — Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal
content:
Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer.
If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE.
If you want the desktop app experience, run
codex app or visit the Codex App page.
If you are looking for the cloud-based agent from OpenAI, Codex Web, go to chatgpt.com/codex.
Run the following on Mac or Linux to install Codex CLI:
curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
Run the following on Windows to install Codex CLI:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex"
The standalone installers download from https://releases.openai.com/codex by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable. To force GitHub Releases, set CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM to false (0 and no are also accepted):
curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh$env:CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM='false'; irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex
Codex CLI can also be installed via the following package managers:
# Install using npm
npm install -g @openai/codex# Install using Homebrew
brew install --cask codex
Then simply run codex to get started.
You can also go to the latest GitHub Release and download the appropriate binary for your platform.
Each GitHub Release contains many executables, but in practice, you likely want one of these:
- macOS
  - Apple Silicon/arm64: codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
  - x86_64 (older Mac hardware): codex-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
- Apple Silicon/arm64: 
- Linux
  - x86_64: codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
  - arm64: codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
- x86_64: 
Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl), so you likely want to rename it to codex after extracting it.
Run codex and select Sign in with ChatGPT. We recommend signing into your ChatGPT account to use Codex as part of your Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan. Learn more about what's included in your ChatGPT plan.
You can also use Codex with an API key, but this requires additional setup.

report.summary: OpenAI releases Codex CLI, an open-source, lightweight coding agent that runs locally in the terminal and integrates with ChatGPT plans.
report.background: Codex CLI arrives amid a wave of agentic coding tools that promise to move AI assistance from chat windows into real development workflows. OpenAI is positioning it as a lightweight, local-first alternative to its cloud-hosted Codex Web agent, letting developers delegate coding tasks directly from the terminal. The release also brings OpenAI back into the open-source fold with an Apache-2.0 license. It supports authentication through standard ChatGPT plans, making it immediately accessible to millions of subscribers, while still offering API-key usage for those outside that ecosystem. Given rising competition from VS Code Copilot agents, Cursor, and open-source terminal agents like Aider, Codex CLI appears designed to lower friction: install it with a one-liner or package manager, sign in, and start issuing coding tasks without leaving the command line.
key_points: Codex CLI runs locally in the terminal rather than in the cloud, making it a lightweight agent for coding tasks that can read, edit, and execute code on the developer's machine.
Installation is designed to be easy and cross-platform: macOS/Linux users get a curl one-liner, Windows users get a PowerShell command, and npm or Homebrew are supported as alternatives.
Users can sign in with their ChatGPT account, and Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plans include Codex capabilities, while API-key access is possible for those who need a separate setup.
The project is open source under Apache-2.0, meaning developers can inspect, modify, and redistribute the code, increasing transparency compared to closed, cloud-only AI coding services.

OpenAI now offers Codex across several surfaces: the local CLI, IDE extensions for VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf, a desktop app experience via the codex app command, and a cloud-based agent on the web.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Codex CLI signals a shift from cloud-hosted AI assistants to local, terminal-native developer agents, likely intensifying competition with open-source tools and IDE-based copilots. Developers benefit from a transparent, open-source agent that fits naturally into their existing command-line workflows, supports multiple install paths, and works with the ChatGPT accounts many already pay for. Regular users who aren't coding may not directly use Codex CLI, but the broader result is faster AI-assisted software development, which can lower the cost and time needed to build the applications they rely on. The Apache-2.0 license also invites community auditing and customization, potentially accelerating innovation in agentic development tools.
report.tools: Watch the openai/codex GitHub repository for releases and documentation. Try installing via npm (@openai/codex) or Homebrew (codex cask). For IDE workflows, look for the Codex extension in VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf. OpenAI also offers the Codex App for desktop and Codex Web at chatgpt.com/codex for cloud-based tasks.
